title: Dental clinic front desk keeps being asked to sign in; admin and user disagree on device state
scenario: An admin reports healthy device registration and a working browser; a receptionist's pasted output and a colleague's browser test say otherwise. The admin later admits his first check ran in his own session; whether the browser really works is never settled.

events.title: Front-desk laptops keep re-asking for Teams sign-in
events.text:
Hi. The front-desk laptops at Penhallow Dental (14 of them) ask for a Teams sign-in every few minutes. I've checked the usual suspects: dsregcmd on the affected laptops I looked at shows AzureAdPrt YES, and the browser version of Teams works fine on all of them, so I don't think it's the devices. Could it be Microsoft's side?

Alun Prys

events.title: Re: Front-desk laptops keep re-asking for Teams sign-in
events.text:
Hi Alun, let's go through it one fact at a time. Please send the exact wording on the laptops, three people it hit with a UTC time for each, and whether other sites are fine. I'd also like the raw dsregcmd /status output from two of the laptops, not a summary; the SSO State block is the part I want.

Bruna

events.title: Re: Front-desk laptops keep re-asking for Teams sign-in
events.text:
Wording: 'Couldn't sign you in, please try again'. People: dana.fox 09:05 UTC, imran.syed 09:21, hettie.wyn 09:40. It's all at this one clinic, our Truro clinic has no trouble. I'll paste dsregcmd when I get a moment - the receptionists are shouting at me.

Alun

events.title: dsregcmd from my laptop
events.text:
Alun said to send you this from my laptop (PEN-FD-03):
| AzureAdJoined : YES
| EnterpriseJoined : NO
| DomainJoined : NO
| Device Name : PEN-FD-03
| AzureAdPrt : NO
| AzureAdPrtAuthority :
| WamDefaultSet : ERROR

Dana Fox

events.title: web version too
events.text:
i tried the web version in edge like alun said and it fails too. same message. so its not just the app

Imran

events.title: Two things that don't fit
events.text:
Alun, two things don't fit together. You reported AzureAdPrt YES and a working browser; Dana's output shows AzureAdPrt NO on PEN-FD-03 and Imran says the browser fails as well. Please run dsregcmd /status in the user's own session (not an elevated prompt signed in as you) on PEN-FD-03 and one other front-desk laptop, and tell me what the AzureAdPrt line says.

Bruna

events.title: Re: Two things that don't fit
events.text:
Ran it again in Dana's own session this time: AzureAdPrt : NO on PEN-FD-03 and NO on PEN-FD-07. My first checks were run in my admin session on those PCs, which showed my own token, so ignore the YES I reported. I haven't looked at the browser question yet.

Alun

events.title: Next step: device registration
events.text:
Right, that clears it up. The front-desk laptops hold no PRT, so silent sign-in can't work; it's a device registration problem. I'm passing it to our identity team to look at the device objects and registration logs for PEN-FD-03 and -07, and I'll write again at 12:00 UTC.

Bruna

events.title: Escalation to identity backend
events.text: Escalation: Penhallow Dental, 14 front-desk laptops prompt repeatedly. dsregcmd in user context on two: AzureAdJoined YES, AzureAdPrt NO. The customer's first report of PRT YES came from the admin's own session and has been withdrawn. Truro clinic unaffected. Ask: registration and PRT acquisition trace for the two device objects.

events.title: Identity team response
events.text: Identity: the 14 device objects were left in a pending state after the clinic's Intune connector was re-linked last week; re-registration triggered from our side. Token acquisition should work after the next sign-in.

events.title: Re: Two things that don't fit
events.text:
Re-registration seems to have worked: dsregcmd in the user session now shows AzureAdPrt : YES on PEN-FD-03 and PEN-FD-07, and Teams stays signed in on all 14 laptops. The browser works as well, I checked on three.

Alun
